P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No. As an EU member state, Romania applies Article 63 TFEU, which prohibits restrictions on capital movements and payments between EU countries and with non-EU countries. Banks still apply AML/KYC checks and may ask for the source of funds.

sources.title: Free movement of capital (European Parliament Fact Sheet)
sources.quote: Article 63 TFEU prohibits all restrictions on the movement of capital and payments between EU countries, as well as between EU and non-EU countries.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. BCR, Romania's largest bank, opens current accounts in lei or foreign currency for individuals free of charge, and its fee schedule for individuals lists a monthly administration fee for a foreign-currency current account (EUR/USD vs other currencies) (BCR fee schedule, valid from 27 January 2018; current fees not checked). EU law (art. 63 TFEU) bars restrictions on capital movements.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A freelancer usually registers a PFA (persoană fizică autorizată) at the trade-register office (ONRC) of the county of the professional seat, before starting activity. You can file online through the ONRC portal with documents signed by qualified electronic signature, or at the counter. Typical documents: ID, proof of the right to use the professional seat (ownership, lease or loan-for-use contract), a declaration that the seat meets operating conditions, and proof of qualification for the chosen CAEN codes. Registration itself is free. A draft fee (200 lei, halved online) was under public debate but not confirmed in force. Processing takes about 1–3 working days when complete.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Tax residents of Romania are taxed on worldwide income (see quoted rules for exceptions such as remittance-basis regimes). Flat 10% generally (not captured). Inference (general source principle, not quoted): work performed while living in Romania for foreign clients is normally taxable in Romania. PFA taxes in 2026 (accounting sources): income tax is 10%, applied to net income after deductible CAS and CASS (or to the income norm, see L7). CAS (pension, 25%) is due once net income reaches 12 minimum wages (48,600 lei). It is charged on a fixed base of 12 wages (12,150 lei) or 24 wages (24,300 lei), not on actual income. CASS (health, 10%) is charged on net income between 6 and 72 minimum wages (2026 maximum 29,160 lei). 2026 thresholds use the 4,050 lei minimum wage in force on 1 January 2026.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: National threshold: the small-business VAT exemption ceiling rose from 300,000 to 395,000 lei on 1 September 2025 (Ordonanța 22/2025). Exceeding it requires VAT registration; the exemption ends with the transaction that crosses it. Operations whose place of supply is not in Romania are no longer counted toward the 395,000 lei. This matters for freelancers: B2B services to foreign businesses (place of supply abroad, see below) do not use up the ceiling. Under the EU SME scheme, businesses under the ceiling can also use exemptions in other member states if EU-wide turnover is at most EUR 100,000. The standard VAT rate is 21%. Under the EU SME scheme, small businesses below a national threshold (at most EUR 85,000) can be exempt on domestic sales. Where services are taxed (EU-wide rules, illustrated by Irish Revenue guidance): (1) B2B, meaning services to business customers in other EU countries or outside the EU, are taxed where the customer is established, so no Romania VAT is charged; EU business customers self-account under the reverse charge. (2) B2C services to private individuals are, as a rule, taxed where the supplier is established, so Romania VAT applies once you are VAT-registered. (3) Exception: consultancy, legal, accounting, engineering, data-processing, advertising, licensing and electronically supplied services to private customers outside the EU are outside EU VAT, subject to 'use and enjoyment' rules. Electronically supplied services to private customers in other EU countries follow special OSS rules (not captured here).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies directly in Romania, supervised by the national data protection authority. It covers EU businesses and non-EU businesses offering goods or services to people in the EU.

sources.title: Data protection (European Commission)
sources.quote: EU data protection legislation is comprised of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the Law Enforcement Directive (LED), and the Data Protection Regulation for EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies (EUDPR).

sources.title: Data protection and online privacy (Your Europe)
sources.quote: These rules apply to both companies and organisations (public and private) in the EU and those based outside the EU who offer goods or services in the EU , such as Facebook or Amazon, whenever these companies request or re-use the personal data of individuals in the EU.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: EU consumer law gives a 14-day withdrawal right for online and distance purchases without justification: 14 days from delivery for goods, and from conclusion of the contract for services. Exceptions include personalised goods, perishables and date-specific services.

sources.title: Returns and the right of withdrawal (Your Europe)
sources.quote: This means you can cancel the contract within 14 days without providing any justification (the "cooling-off period").

sources.title: Returns and the right of withdrawal (Your Europe)
sources.quote: For goods this means 14 days from the date of delivery, for services 14 days after the day the contract was agreed.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Income norm (normă de venit): for activities on the official list, PFA income tax is 10% of a fixed annual income norm set per activity and county, not of actual profit. Threshold: anyone whose 2025 gross receipts exceeded the lei equivalent of EUR 25,000 (126,037 lei at the 2025 average rate) must use the real system (actual income minus expenses) from 2026. Whether a given online/IT activity is on the norm list depends on the CAEN code and county (not captured). Contabilul.manager.ro confirms the EUR 25,000 rule (Fiscal Code art. 69(9)): exceeding it moves you to the real system from the following year.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
